title: CTA — Move the Viewer
summary: One CTA aligned with one video goal — clear, simple, and directly useful to the viewer.

sections.heading: Orientation — Lesson Start
sections.subtitle: Lesson Start
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **What Will You Understand?** **CTA (Call to Action)** — If it’s **not present**, the viewer **will leave** — **even if** the video is **good**.
- **Goal:** To ask for **one useful step** for the viewer **and for you** — **not** just «Like, everyone». 
- **What’s Next After the Lesson?** You will write **ready-to-publish CTAs** that match **the goal of each video**.

sections.heading: Tension — The Problem
sections.subtitle: The Problem
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **Too many requests** **confuse** the viewer.
- «Follow me **and** like **and** comment **and** share **and** save» — **at the same time** — so **often** they do **nothing**.
- **Pressure** **without value** shows **quickly** — and **reduces trust** in the content.

sections.heading: Core Idea — Choose One CTA Based on the Video Goal
sections.subtitle: Choose One CTA Based on the Video Goal
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **Each video** has **one goal:** **Engagement**, **Save and Share**, or **Sales Conversation**.
- A **strong CTA (Call to Action)** combines **three** things: **clear**, **easy to execute**, and **direct benefit** to the viewer.
- **Is your goal to build an audience?** Ask a **real question** that encourages people to **respond with experience**.
- **Is your goal useful sharing?** Ask for a **specific Save** or **Share** — **Save/Share CTA**.
- **Is your goal Leads (people showing interest who may become customers)?** Ask for a **direct message** with a **clear word** **and a next step** — **Lead CTA**.

sections.heading: Comparison — General Request or Intentional Step?
sections.subtitle: General Request or Intentional Step?
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Distracting Approach | Smart Approach |
|----------------|---------------|
| «If you **like** it, do **everything**» — a **general** request **not linked** to a goal — **weak result** | «Send me the word **Plan** in **DM (Direct Message)** so I can send you the **template**» — **one request**, **clear**, **linked to value** |

sections.heading: Glossary — 3 Terms Are Enough
sections.subtitle: 3 Terms Are Enough
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---------|--------|------|
| **CTA (Call to Action)** | The phrase that **asks** the viewer for a **step** after the video | «Write the **biggest challenge** you face in the **first week**» |
| **Save/Share CTA** | A request to **save** or **share** when the content is **referenceable** and useful **later** | «**Save** the video **and send it** to someone who **can benefit** from it» |
| **Lead CTA** | A **direct** request that opens a **conversation** with **Leads (people showing interest)** | «Send the word **Offer** in **DM** so I can send you the **details**» |

sections.heading: Quiz — Quick Confirmation
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
> **Quiz key (unchanged):** correctIndex: 1

**Question:** If the video **explains a useful brief method** — and the most suitable **goal** is for people to **return** to it **later** and **send it** to those who **need it** — which **CTA** is **best**?

«If you **like** it, do **like** and **follow** and **comment** **now**».
«**Save** the video **and send it** to someone **who may benefit** from it».
«Send me a **DM now** to book a **call**».

**Explanation:** This **CTA** is **linked** **to the content goal**: **Save and Share** — **without pressure** and **without distraction**.

sections.heading: Mission — Write 3 Ready-to-Publish CTAs
sections.subtitle: Write 3 Ready-to-Publish CTAs
sections.contentMarkdown:
**Introduction:** Write **3 CTAs** **for the same content idea:** **one question**, **one save or share**, **one lead in DM**. The goal is to **distinguish** between them and choose the **right one** based on your **goal**.

**Submission:** Video Idea · CTA Question · CTA Save/Share · CTA Lead · Which one in the final version and why

**Evaluation Criteria:**

| Dimension | Weight | Criterion |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Clarity of Wording | 50% | Each **CTA** has a **clear** and **understandable action** |
| Relevance to Goal | 50% | The **final choice** is **justified** **by the video goal** |
